The esraj is a bowed string instrument of South Asia, a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.321-71. It is a modern variant of the dilruba, with a neck like a sitar's, metal frets and several sympathetic strings, and four main strings, played with a bow, able to slide to imitate the turns of the human voice. When played the body usually rests on the lap or the floor with the neck against the shoulder; in the Santiniketan tradition it stands upright on the leg. It is found in the Sikh music of Pakistan and of the Punjab in North India, and is also used in the Rabindra songs and classical music of Bangladesh and West Bengal.
以斯拉吉琴為南亞弦鳴樂器，見於巴基斯坦與北印度旁遮普的錫克音樂，以及孟加拉與西孟: The esraj is a chordophone of South Asia, found in the Sikh music of Pakistan and the Punjab in North India, and in the classical music and Rabindra songs of Bangladesh and West Bengal; at the music faculty of Visva-Bharati University in Santiniketan, Tagore made it compulsory for students, so it often accompanies traditional Rabindra songs. It also came into the Sikh kirtan line-up through the Gurmatt Sangeet movement. In George Harrison's 'Within You Without You' it was played by musicians of the Asian Music Circle.
以斯拉吉琴為弓拉弦鳴樂器，金屬弦經山羊皮共鳴板發聲，並有十二至十五條共鳴弦。若裝: The esraj is a bowed chordophone; its metal strings sound through a goatskin soundboard, and it has twelve to fifteen sympathetic strings. If two or three jawari strings are fitted, it can produce a sharper sound. The player bows the strings and stops them with the left hand on the metal frets, sliding up and down to make a meend. The esraj has four main strings; compared with the dilruba it has fewer main strings, fewer sympathetic strings and a differently shaped body.
以斯拉吉琴的弦全部為金屬製，包括主弦與共鳴弦，琴頸上另有二十根金屬品柱。發聲面板: All the strings of the esraj are metal, both the main and the sympathetic strings, and there are twenty metal frets on the neck. The soundboard is of stretched goatskin, similar to the sarangi's. The source does not state the material of the body and neck, but the long frame that carries the sympathetic strings is of wood. Some instruments have a gourd fitted at the top to balance or to strengthen the tone. The new-style body made at Santiniketan is larger and has a hole in the back, and there is a detachable resonating part behind the head whose material the source does not describe.
以斯拉吉琴約有三百年的歷史，是迪爾魯巴琴的現代變體。迪爾魯巴琴由第十代錫克教祖師: The esraj is about three hundred years old and is a modern variant of the dilruba. The dilruba was adapted by the tenth Sikh guru, Guru Gobind Singh, from the taus so that the Khalsa soldiers could carry it on horseback. The instrument is found in Pakistan, the Punjab in North India, Bangladesh and West Bengal, used in Sikh music, Rabindra songs and classical music. It declined in the later twentieth century and had almost disappeared in the 1980s; it recovered after the Gurmatt Sangeet movement revived the Sikh chanting line-up. Rabindranath Tagore made it compulsory at the music faculty of Visva-Bharati University, and it became the main accompanying instrument of traditional Rabindra songs.
演奏時可跪坐將琴夾於兩膝間，或坐姿置於膝上，也可放於身前地面，琴頸靠左肩；尚提尼: You can kneel and hold the instrument between the knees, rest it on the lap when sitting, or set it on the floor in front of you with the neck against the left shoulder; players at Santiniketan stand it upright on the leg. It sounds when the bow is drawn across the main strings while the other hand moves on the metal frets, sliding up and down for meend and imitating the vibrato of the voice; the middle finger can be used for the krintan technique. A beginner should first fix the angle at which the instrument is held, then practise bowing, stopping at the frets, slides and ornaments.
